"Briefly" always signals shortness — but there are two kinds of shortness it can refer to: shortness in time, and shortness in expression (words used). Once you understand this, the word clicks into place instantly.
Meaning 1 — For a Short Time

When "briefly" modifies a physical action or a state, it tells you that something happened, but it didn't last long. The action occurred, and then it was over quickly.

  • "The sun briefly appeared from behind the clouds." → The sun came out, but only for a moment before it was gone again.
  • "She briefly worked as a teacher before becoming a lawyer." → She was a teacher, but not for very long.
  • "He briefly glanced at the paper." → He looked at it for just a second.

This meaning answers the question: How long did this last? Answer: not long.
Meaning 2 — In Few Words / Concisely

When "briefly" modifies how someone speaks, writes, or explains something, it means they did so without going into great detail — they kept it short and to the point.

  • "Can you briefly explain the situation?" → Explain it, but don't give me every single detail.
  • "She briefly mentioned the problem during the meeting." → She brought it up, but didn't dwell on it.
  • "The report briefly covered the main points." → It touched on them without going deep.

This meaning answers the question: How much was said or written? Answer: not much.
"Briefly" at the Start of a Sentence

You'll sometimes see "briefly" placed right at the beginning of a sentence. Here, it functions as a signal to the reader, meaning: "What follows is a short summary."

  • "Briefly, the company is in financial trouble." → In short, here's the quick version.
  • "Briefly, this is how the system works." → Let me say this in a few words.

This is simply the second meaning applied to an entire statement.
The One Idea Behind Both Meanings

Both meanings share a single underlying idea: you are getting less than the full thing. Whether it's about time (the event was shorter than it could have been) or words (fewer were used than could have been), "briefly" always signals a condensed, trimmed-down version of something.
How to Tell Which Meaning Is Being Used

Look at the verb it's attached to. If it's a physical action or state — visited, appeared, lived, paused, stopped — then "briefly" is about time. If it's about speaking, writing, or explaining — mentioned, explained, described, discussed, summarised — then "briefly" is about expression (few words).

Worth noting: both meanings can blend together. "She briefly described the plan" means she used few words and it was over quickly. Both can be true at once.
The Polite Use — A Subtle but Important Nuance

"Briefly" is often used as a polite signal meaning: I won't take up too much of your time. It works to reassure the listener that whatever is coming will be small and not burdensome.

  • "Can I briefly ask you something?" → I have a question, and I promise it won't take long.
  • "I'll briefly go over the rules." → I'll cover them quickly, without dragging it out.

This makes "briefly" a useful word for being considerate and respectful of others' time in conversation.
"Briefly" vs. "Shortly" — A Common Confusion

These two words look similar, but they mean very different things.

"Shortly" usually means soon — at a near point in the future. "The doctor will see you shortly" means the doctor will see you soon.

"Briefly" means for a short time or in few words. It's not about when something happens, but about how long it lasts or how concisely it's delivered. "The doctor briefly examined her" means the examination itself was quick.

The key test: if you can replace the word with "soon," it's "shortly." If you can replace it with "for a short time" or "in a few words," it's "briefly."
Synonyms

For the time meaning: momentarily, fleetingly, for a moment, for a short while, in passing.

For the expression meaning: concisely, succinctly, in short, in a nutshell.
Antonyms

For the time meaning: at length, for a long time, for an extended period, extensively.

For the expression meaning: in detail, thoroughly, at length, elaborately, exhaustively.
Common Word Pairings

"Briefly" pairs naturally with certain verbs. Knowing these will make the word feel natural to use:

For communication: briefly mention, briefly note, briefly explain, briefly describe, briefly discuss, briefly summarise, briefly touch on.

For physical action: briefly visit, briefly appear, briefly stop, briefly pause, briefly hesitate, briefly look.
The Bottom Line

"Briefly" = short. Either something happened for a short time, or it was said/written in a short way. That's the whole word. Every use of "briefly" you will ever encounter falls into one of these two meanings, or into a blend of both.
